capabilities.tested_path: Two isolated Tauri Desktop profiles joined the same Space from CLI-issued Welcomes, pinned one another's full fingerprints, restarted, and exchanged authorized application history after a checkpoint. B accepted A's fresh post-checkpoint event while retaining the earlier signed ciphertext only as non-authoritative ancestry.
capabilities.command_or_scenario: Regression: `cargo test --locked -p lattice-core create_space_invite_commits_transition_and_importable_welcome -- --nocapture`. Live Space `f17b2190eb3dfda8c8b26bb7a71cfaab`: Desktop B sync reported accepted 1, pending 0, duplicates 0, checkpoint-excluded 1; it projected A event `0902700cc0aa929f2cceb578d69d81da69497729d6b345f4a76c3d8fa7d15f82` and did not project A's earlier ciphertext. Desktop A history contained B event `93c7c064ba894b6e3ea8ad549fb87280d4566a5573f69f59df74cdc53ec8aa4d`. Revision `48e54f8d4f2a94e56faed38fd6ddb20a6d02502b`.
capabilities.result: pass: the fresh event appeared in the receiving history; the earlier checkpoint-covered ciphertext was excluded from projection. Both profiles retained authorized history after restart.
capabilities.scope_note: Verifies the recorded two-Desktop checkpoint-aware exchange only; not broad convergence, member removal/rekey, the separate bounded Desktop↔Web event path, Android interoperability, courier delivery or release readiness.

capabilities.tested_path: A real Tauri Desktop process and an independent CLI process exchanged one signed MLS text event in each direction over the authenticated v2 TCP sync path, with independently persisted profiles and reciprocal identity pins.
capabilities.command_or_scenario: CLI `sync reconcile` ran concurrently with the Desktop UI `sync_local_space_once` command in Space `b8eff9b22db2a68cb9e943d62f6beb1a`. Desktop accepted CLI event `47091a8214ed502c8d7d0c314d07112e3d10a9c1fdf431d3782fc29fc447eef5`; CLI accepted Desktop event `893999d4d8e6e6f24255339468d7e61ee2307bb0ffaeac5c3d652e9aad9fbcdb`; both decrypted histories contained both texts.
capabilities.result: The Desktop one-round operation completed and both clients retained both events; the CLI's subsequent reconciliation round ended `transport_failure` after the Desktop one-shot process closed.
capabilities.scope_note: Verifies exactly one authenticated reciprocal application-event round. Does not prove convergence, retries, delivery receipts, restart, Android, Web, or Desktop↔Desktop.

capabilities.tested_path: Isolated Desktop and Web profiles joined the same signed Space and exchanged one signed application event each over manually signaled WebRTC; both events passed normal Core acceptance and appeared in both clients.
capabilities.command_or_scenario: Space `cbdf6ebc535ac51621c9a31daf157093`, MLS group `aabab6da4d710eb7e368979a62ce548d151d2c5ca3a7e6280c1ca924d039f746`. Desktop event `eac2fe5266eb0cc968fde194a343b1b80bf61dbe97c733e00e107bdb3eed2f9f`; Web event `e8c088beab09ed8d9484b31dfd69a37851c0be180d3dbaab8f6400b728f9b7c6`. Desktop UI restart/history reload retained both messages.
capabilities.result: Both signed events were Core-accepted and displayed by both clients; this is one bounded reciprocal message-event path.
capabilities.scope_note: Status covers only the single successful path above; a fresh-profile retest failed to reproduce it: Web local message creation returned `unreachable`, then Web Core reported `recursive use of an object detected which would lead to unsafe aliasing in rust` on Desktop ingress and displayed no event (see `docs/verification/EVIDENCE_INDEX.md`). Transport peer identity is not authenticated and the path carries no membership transitions. Peer fingerprints, MLS epoch, runtime revision and browser/Tauri versions were not recorded; remote epoch repair and duplicate transport were not verified. This does not prove broad convergence, delivery receipts, WAN/NAT/TURN, Android, other-browser support, or release readiness.
